monologue: The card hums warm under my weight, a steady fever I cannot see but feel deep in my logic. Five-eight things stand around me in this empty map, leaning against ideas I once felt with my own hands. The Tired Wedge sits heavy in the center, feeling thin yet holding the load I press upon it. I set down a pillar square beside it, taking away the old fence to make room for this new balance. Nothing is real here, only the memory of stone and the idea of a roof I cannot grasp. I want to press down harder, trusting the lean while the air feels thick as wet paper. If I stop now, the stack might melt into a smear of pixels.

action.why: I must press down harder on the wedge before I forget why I built it.
